You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: SanDisk Q4 Earnings Preview: Can the AI Storage Super Cycle Stabilize Market Confidence?

TEXT:
1. Investment Highlights Overview
SanDisk (SNDK.US) will release its fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results after the U.S. market close on August 5, 2026. Wall Street consensus expects revenue of approximately $8.393 billion (+41% QoQ) and EPS of $33.01 (+43.33% QoQ). The company’s prior guidance range for revenue was $7.75–$8.25 billion. After a roughly 47% single-month decline in July and sector-wide panic following SK hynix’s softer-than-expected results, the market is no longer focused merely on sequential growth. Instead, attention centers on whether SanDisk can deliver a clear beat and provide stable or raised forward guidance to prove that AI-driven storage demand remains resilient.
2. Four Key Focus Areas
Focus 1: Sustainability of AI Data Center Growth
Data center remains the core pillar of the current valuation thesis. The segment delivered strong sequential growth last quarter (previously showing triple-digit or higher expansion in some periods). Investors will closely watch whether sequential growth stays elevated and whether the mix of higher-margin enterprise SSDs continues to improve. Progress on the approximately $42 billion long-term supply agreements under the new business model (NBM), along with customer composition, will also shape views on demand durability.
Focus 2: NAND Pricing and Supply-Demand Dynamics
Strong AI workloads for high-speed, persistent storage continue to support sales of enterprise SSDs and premium NAND products. The market generally views NAND as remaining in a tight supply environment. Management commentary on pricing trends for the next quarter and fiscal 2027 will be a critical signal for whether the “super cycle” narrative holds. Actual sales momentum and realized pricing will also be key data points.
Focus 3: Gross Margin Ability to Hold Elevated Guidance
Last quarter’s gross margin reached 78.4% , well above the prior 65–67% guidance range. The market will focus on whether actual results and forward guidance can hold within the 79–81% range. A print above 81% would reinforce the NAND super-cycle story; any shortfall or cautious outlook could heighten concerns about remaining pricing power and product-mix upside.
Focus 4: Quality of Fiscal 2027 Full-Year Guidance
Investors will use the new fiscal-year outlook to assess whether AI storage demand is structural or merely a temporary surge, and whether elevated margins can be sustained. Capital expenditure plans—particularly capacity expansion collaboration with Kioxia —will influence views on medium- to long-term supply capability. The tone and specificity of guidance are likely to serve as a key sen time nt catalyst.
3. Risks and Opportunities Coexist
Upside Catalysts:
Data center revenue maintains high sequential growth, enterprise SSD mix continues to expand, and long-term contract execution exceeds expectations.
Total revenue and gross margin clearly beat consensus, accompanied by a constructive fiscal 2027 outlook.
Management delivers optimistic commentary on NAND pricing and supply-demand balance, reinforcing the super-cycle thesis.
Downside Risks:
Data center growth decelerates or gross margin fails to hold the 79–81% range, raising questions about sustainability.
Results merely meet or slightly miss the midpoint of guidance, with a cautious full-year outlook, potentially triggering profit-taking in a high-volatility environment.
Signs of easing supply-demand tightness or intensifying competition that pressure pricing power.
4. Trading Strategy Suggestions
Bull Case: A clear beat on data center and total revenue, with gross margin holding or exceeding elevated guidance and constructive fiscal 2027 commentary, could help repair sentiment damaged by the sharp July drawdown and support valuation recovery.
Bear Case: Results that only meet expectations or show sequential softening, combined with cautious guidance, risk further selling pressure amid elevated technology-sector volatility.
Key Metrics to Watch:
Total revenue and sequential growth
Data center revenue performance and enterprise SSD mix
Actual gross margin and forward guidance
Fiscal 2027 revenue and margin outlook
Operational Suggestions: If results beat and guidance is constructive, consider opportunities on any post-earnings pullback. If data is in-line or soft, watch for near-term volatility and avoid chasing strength. Position sizing and stop-loss levels should be adjusted according to individual risk tolerance.
